subject: Route-level cost attribution + alerting proposal
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: sales@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Route-level cost attribution + alerting proposal

Hi team —

Following up from last week's product sync: Nimbus (pilot customer) asked for the ability to see cost and latency attribution by "route"/API endpoint (they want per-route token spend, 95/99 latency percentiles, and alerting when cost per minute exceeds a threshold). They framed it as a must-have for their finance and SRE teams before committing to Dedicated.

High-level ask: can we surface a per-route dashboard in Console that includes
- total tokens / minute broken down by route (day/week/30d)
- cost attribution (estimated $ by route using current pricing)
- latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) and recent regressions
- anomaly alerts (email/Slack) for sudden cost spikes or latency degradation

Constraints / notes:
- Nimbus wants 90-day retention for the per-route breakdown (they said finance needs historical trends).
- We should show both hosted and dedicated usage where applicable.
- Keep an eye on the cardinality problem if customers create many ad-hoc routes.

I've attached a quick mock (route-cost-example.csv) and a short spec (req-spec-observability.md). Can product + console engineering review feasibility and rough ETA? Marcus, can you scope and prioritize relative to the Q2 console backlog? Laura/Vivek, any immediate red flags on the ingestion/metrics side?

Thanks —
Stephanie

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions & GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route-level cost attribution + alerting proposal

Thanks Steph — this looks actionable. Quick reactions and questions: 

1) Priority & scope: we have a Q2 epics list that includes "per-model dashboards" and "cost breakdowns" but not explicitly per-route. We can treat "per-route" as an extension of per-model if we define a route->model mapping. Need clarity on default route taxonomy (path, tag, or explicit route id).

2) Tradeoffs: computing cost attribution in near real-time could be expensive if we recompute token-level costs on ingest. Options:
  - materialize route-level aggregates at write-time (cheaper read, more write cost)
  - compute on demand with cached results (cheaper writes, higher read latency for large queries)

3) Retention & privacy: 90d retention for aggregates seems fine. Keeping per-request traces for 90d is questionable and will increase storage + egress. Are we only keeping aggregated counters?

4) Alerts: we should support threshold and anomaly detection (statistical) as two modes. Anomaly mode needs a baseline window; this could be expensive to compute if we don't pre-aggregate.

Action items for me: I'll draft a PRD with two implementation options (materialized vs on-demand aggregation) and a rough cost delta. Can we get a short runbook from Console Eng on where the route identifiers live and how customers currently tag routes? Laura — can you send that by EOD Wed?

—Marcus
Product Manager

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, infra-observability@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route-level cost attribution + alerting proposal

Summary of feasibility from Console/Telemetry side:

- Route identifiers: we currently log a "route_name" tag for SDK and API proxy calls for ~85% of traffic. The remaining traffic has ad-hoc client-defined paths (high cardinality). We can normalize by introducing a recommended route header (x-rw-route) for customers to set.

- Aggregation strategy: materialized aggregates at ingest (per-minute buckets) is the most efficient for alerting and p95/p99 queries — it costs more in write throughput but keeps query latency low. On-demand compute will be costlier for heavy queries and will complicate alerting.

- Retention: 90-day retention for aggregates is fine. Storing full request-level logs for 90 days will increase S3/GCS costs ~x3 and requires a privacy/contract exception. For Nimbus specifically, we could offer a "historical aggregates" add-on and mark full request-level retention as an enterprise opt-in.

- Implementation estimate (rough):
  Phase 1 (6 weeks): schema updates, per-minute materialized aggregates, per-route dashboard UI prototyping, simple threshold-based alerts
  Phase 2 (4 weeks): anomaly detection service (rolling baseline), per-customer cost multiplier (pricing integration), retention controls in Console

Blocks / needs:
  - Legal/security sign-off for any extended retention or per-request trace exports.
  - Billing integration to convert tokens->$ (need Pricing Eng input).
  - Product decision on default route taxonomy (path vs header).

I'll open OBS-7621 with the technical design and a more detailed estimate.

Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager, Console

From: Lara O'Neill <lara.oneill@nimbus.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@nimbus.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route-level cost attribution + alerting proposal

Stephanie —

Thanks for flagging this. Quick feedback from our side:
- 90-day historical trend is non-negotiable for our procurement team; they need month-over-month attribution.
- We prefer a header-based route id (we can standardize on x-rw-route) to avoid path cardinality issues. We can push this change in our SDK integration quickly.
- For alerts: email to billing and a Slack webhook to our SRE channel is required.

If Redwood can commit to Phase 1 in ~6 weeks we can move forward on Dedicated onboarding. Happy to jump on a sync with Marcus + Laura to finalize the scope.

Best,
Lara O'Neill
Head of Platform
Nimbus Analytics

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route-level cost attribution + alerting proposal

All — thanks for the quick turn. Plan of record:

1) Marcus: please file a short PRD by Monday that picks the materialized-aggregate path as default but calls out the on-demand alternative for very-low-traffic tenants. Link OBS-7621 in the PRD.

2) Laura/Vivek: start Phase 1 workstream (schema + per-minute aggregates + UI prototype + threshold alerts). Your 6-week ETA is baseline; if there are infra blockers raise immediately.

3) Contracts/Legal: quick check for a limited enterprise retention exception for Nimbus (90d aggregates only; no full request-level raw logs unless they pay for the add-on). CC'ing contracts.

4) Nimbus: implement x-rw-route in SDK; Steph will coordinate a short integration test.

Action items and owners attached in the Drive doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/observability/route-cost-proposal and Jira OBS-7621. I'll run a short kickoff on Monday 10am PT to align owners and success criteria (metrics: correct per-route cost within 2% vs invoiced, p99 latency available under 60s query latency).

—Stephanie
